Forestry needed daily irrigation from urban canals

In Weaver's method, the theoretical standard splits 100% evenly among k crops: 100% for monoculture (1 crop), 50% each for 2-crop, 33.33% each for 3-crop, 25% each for 4-crop, and minimizes σ² = Σ(d_i)² / n.

प्रश्न (हिंदी संस्करण): In Alfred Weber's (1909) Least-Cost Theory of Industrial Location, the 'Material Index' (MI) is defined as the ratio of:
optionsEn: Weight of localized (weight-losing) raw materials to the weight of the finished product
Weight of ubiquities (water/air) to total labor cost
Transport cost of finished goods to agglomeration savings
Total capital investment to weight of raw materials

questions.explanationEn: Weber defined Material Index MI = (Weight of localized raw materials) / (Weight of finished product). Weber defined Material Index MI = (Weight of localized raw materials) / (Weight of finished product). If MI > 1 (weight-losing industry like iron smelting or sugar milling), the optimal plant location is pulled toward the raw material source; if MI ≤ 1, it locates at the market.

optionsEn: A Functionally Interdependent System of Cities (polycentric urban-industrial integration with minimized regional disparity)
Pre-industrial independent local centers with no hierarchy
A single primate core dominating an exploited periphery
Complete de-urbanization back to subsistence farming

Friedmann's 4 stages are: (1) Pre-industrial independent local centers, (2) Transitional single strong core + periphery, (3) Industrializing single core + sub-cores, and (4) Post-industrial functionally interdependent polycentric urban system.

Sea Power Theory of Alfred Thayer Mahan
